**Half Life:**

Half-life refers to the time taken for plasma concentration of a drug fall by 50% 

- most relevant to single compartment model 
- Exponential process related to volume of distribution and inversely proportion to clearance

T1/2 = 0.693xVd / Cl 

In  multi compartment model the t1/2 may refer to the distribution or terminal elimination half time 

- T/2a Distribution half time 
- T1/2b Elimination half time 

![](/content/exams/anzca/2015/B/4/standard-image14.jpeg){fig-alt="Distribution and elimination half-lives in a multicompartment model"}

**Context Sensitive Half Time (CSHT):**

CHHT refers to the time taken for plasma drug concentration to fall by 50% of its value after cessation of an infusion, in context of the duration of the infusion.

For drugs described by single compartment models this is the half time, however all anaesthetic drugs are multi compartment 

CHST determinants:

- duration of the infusion and therefore saturation of the peripheral compartments 
- redistribution between peripheral and central compartments
- clearance from the central compartment  

**Differences between Half-life and CSHT**

CHST describes the elimination kinetics from the central compartment in a multi compartment model. It has no fixed number and varies depending on infusion duration →‘context’

- in short infusion times CSHT = t1/2a the redistribution half time
- in longer infusions CSHT = t1/2b the terminal elimination half time 

**Relevant Examples**

**Fentanyl Vs Remifentanil** 

+-------------------+--------------+-----------------------------------+
| **Parameter**     | **Fentanyl** | **Remifentanil**                  |
+===================+==============+===================================+
| **Vd**            | 4l/Kg        | 0.3l/kg                           |
+-------------------+--------------+-----------------------------------+
| **CL**            | 17ml/kg/min  | 70ml/kg/min                       |
|                   |              |                                   |
|                   | Hepatic      | Plasma and tissue cholinesterase  |
+-------------------+--------------+-----------------------------------+
| **t1/2a**         | 1.5min       | 1min                              |
+-------------------+--------------+-----------------------------------+
| **CSHT 10min**    | 12 min       | 3 min                             |
+-------------------+--------------+-----------------------------------+
| **CSHT 3 hours ** | 70 min       | 3 min                             |
+-------------------+--------------+-----------------------------------+

Both fentanyl and remifentanil have rapid t1/2a times and redistribute rapidly. However fentanyl is far more lipophilic and so has larger volume of distribution.

Remifentanil has a small Vd and undergoes metabolism in tissue and plasma and so results is rapid clearance. 

Fentanyl redistributes from peripheral compartments which results in longer terminal elimination time / CSHT.

**Propofol Vs Thiopentone** 

+-------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------+
| **Parameter**     | **Thiopentone**                                                                        | **Propofol**                                         |
+===================+========================================================================================+======================================================+
| **Vd**            | 2l/Kg                                                                                  | 4l/kg                                                |
+-------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------+
| **CL**            | Low hepatic extraction ratio rapid enzymatic saturation→ 1st order - 0 order kinetics  | High Hepatic extraction ratio →first order kinetics  |
|                   |                                                                                        |                                                      |
|                   | C                                                                                      | CL 30ml/kg/min                                       |
+-------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------+
| **t1/2a**         | 1.5min                                                                                 | 2min                                                 |
+-------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------+
| **CSHT 10min**    | 4 min                                                                                  | 5 min                                                |
+-------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------+
| **CSHT 3 hours ** | 85 min                                                                                 | 9 min                                                |
+-------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------+

Thiopentone has a rapid onset and rapid offset due to distribution with t1/2a 8min. However, the hepatic enzymatic metabolism can rapidly become saturated so clearance is low resulting in a long CSHT. 

Propofol also has rapid onset and offset due to redistribution and a large Vd. However relatively short CSHT due to high clearance of 30ml/kg/min and first order kinetics result in significantly shorter CSHT.
